Question: How can I optimize my BGN page for the Enterprise Search?
Answer:
There are different ways to optimize BGN pages for your search engine via the "Edit page":

    Title/Heading
    We recommend to choose a significant title/headline which also can be found in the text of the page, e.g.: Instead of "About BD/PWS3" a title like "Application Release Management (BD/PWS3)" should be used


    Keywords
    The use of good keywords increases the chance to be found at the top of the hit list.
        If keywords are entered in the fields 'Keywords' they have to be divided by commas: "Enterprise Search, Suche Wiki"
        Department Keyword Stating your department can also lead to better results if a user is looking for information on your department in particular, e.g.: BD/WPA-WCS4, BD/WPA. It is also recommended to include former department names so users can find you after re-organization activities.


    Description
    The page should consist of continuous text and not only of keywords. But keywords and the headline/title should again be part of the text.
AB Answer:
To optimize your BGN page for the Enterprise Search, you can follow these steps:

    Title/Heading: Choose a significant title/headline that can also be found in the text of the page. For example, instead of "About BD/PWS3," use a title like "Application Release Management (BD/PWS3)."
    Keywords: Use good keywords to increase the chance of being found at the top of the hit list. Enter keywords in the "Keywords" field, separated by commas. For example, "Enterprise Search, Suche Wiki."
    Department Keyword: Include your department name to improve search results for users looking for information on your department. It is also recommended to include former department names for users to find you after re-organization activities.
    Description: The page should consist of continuous text, not just keywords. However, keywords and the headline/title should be part of the text.

Please note that these optimization principles also apply to Docupedia and other systems.

Question: How to respond to suspicious e-mails
Answer:
Was muss ich tun, wenn ich eine Junk Mail in meinem Posteingang erhalte?  

Bitte seien Sie immer vorsichtig, wenn Sie e-Mails von unbekannten Absendern erhalten. Sollten Sie sich unsicher sein,

    klicken Sie nicht auf einen Link
    öffnen Sie keine Anhänge
    antworten Sie dem Absender nicht
    laden Sie keine Bilder runter

Um solche E-Mails zu melden, nutzen Sie den Report Spam Button:
AB Answer:
To respond to suspicious emails, follow these steps:

    Do not click on any links or download any attachments in the email.
    Do not provide any personal or sensitive information requested in the email.
    Mark the email as spam or phishing, depending on your email provider.
    Delete the email from your inbox and trash folder.
    If you are unsure about the legitimacy of the email, contact the sender directly using a verified contact method to confirm its authenticity.
    Report the suspicious email to your IT department or email provider for further investigation.

Remember to always exercise caution when dealing with suspicious emails to protect your personal information and prevent potential security breaches.

Question: Who can give access to a sharepoint?
Answer: Site owner
Context_paragraphs:
SharePoint on premises

Relevant for:  SITE OWNER  

To grant full access to a site, its documents, folders, lists, site menu functions, ribbon functions etc., you can add users to one of the predefined standard groups. Each group has its own permissions and the members of the group will have access to all items and functions with the permissions the group have, as long as the default permissions are not changed by owners. 

By default the following standard groups are predefined in each SharePoint site:

    Visitors (Read only permission)
    Members (Read/Write/Delete permission)
    Owners (Read/Write/Delete permission, Administrate site and site groups)
    Project Manager (Read/Write/Delete + overwrite list behavior (to undo check-out & "Lock" for other users))
    Access Right Owner – ARO; previously called: Master of Role - MoR (Read)
        as ARO / MoR a WOM organization has to be entered

Own created SharePoint groups don't get access to the full site but can only be permitted on apps (lists & libraries).

Question: What is an Internet Based Client?
Answer: Currently, the computers are provisioned in Bosch Network (Intranet). In order to adapt the change in way of working and use cases, we designed a new end-device configuration, Internet-based Client (IBC). IBC is a future-proof end device which is provisioned on the Internet. It enables direct and secure connection to internal and external applications which you need daily basis.
AB Answer: An Internet-based Client (IBC) is a future-proof end device that is provisioned on the Internet. It enables a direct and secure connection to internal and external applications that are needed on a daily basis. The IBC is designed to adapt to the changing ways of working and use cases, allowing users to work anywhere efficiently. It has key features such as SASE-enabled, client perimeter security concept, self-guided installation process for Windows, and the ability to order new, re-install current computers, or install as a virtual machine. The IBC also implements client lifecycle management via Intune.

Answer: No
AB Answer: No, strictly confidential (SC-3) data is not allowed on OneDrive.
Context_paragraphs:
How to store C-SC3 data on your assigned laptop while using OneDrive OneDrive Sync Client?

C-SC3 data in not allowed in OneDrive. Only data which is classified below C-SC3 can be stored in OneDrive. To avoid the risk of accidental upload of C-SC3 data in OneDrive while Syncing known folders, please create a folder under C:\Users\UserID\FolderName e.g. C:\Users\kxx1mtp\Secured. 

Folders created at this location are secured for logged in user only and is not synced to OneDrive

Question: How can I exchange data using adhoc?

Question: What is Wifi calling?
Answer: Wi-Fi Calling is a mobile telephony service over Wi-Fi.
AB Answer: Wi-Fi Calling is a mobile telephony service that allows users to make and receive calls over a Wi-Fi network instead of using the mobile operator's radio network. It enables users to make calls even in areas with poor or no mobile coverage, such as locations with thick concrete walls or special glass facades. Wi-Fi Calling offers fast call setup times, HD-Voice quality, and the same call behavior as normal calls with the default smartphone dialer and phone number. It does not require any additional apps like Skype or WhatsApp. Wi-Fi Calling is already included in the user's mobile tariff and can be used for both private and emergency calls.
Context_paragraphs:
What is Wi-Fi Calling?   

Wi-Fi Calling is a mobile telephony service over Wi-Fi. In this case, the call is placed over the Wi-Fi access points instead of mobile operator's radio network and thereby users will be able to make and receive calls, also at locations where there is no sufficient mobile coverage. If your smartphone is connected to a Wi-Fi network, it establishes a connection to the operators core network. Your smartphone remembers already known Wi-Fi networks. If you are in the vicinity, it connects automatically and you make calls via Wi-Fi depending on the priority given by your operator. Some operator prioritizes Wi-Fi Calling over normal calls and some vice versa.

Question: How can I recall a message sent with Outlook?
Answer:
Steps to recall an email:

    Navigate to the <Sent Items> folder
    Double-click to open the desired message for the callback
    Click on <File> on the top left, select menu item <Info>, in the area <Message Send and Recall> select <Recall this message> 

In the dialog box that appears, select either <Delete copies of this message> or <Delete and replace with a new message>, then click OK.
Context_paragraphs:
How do I use the new message callback feature?

As the sender of an e-mail that I want to call back, the Windows Outlook client must be used for the callback.

Steps to recall an email:

    Navigate to the <Sent Items> folder
    Double-click to open the desired message for the callback
    Click on <File> on the top left, select menu item <Info>, in the area <Message Send and Recall> select <Recall this message> 

In the dialog box that appears, select either <Delete copies of this message> or <Delete and replace with a new message>, then click OK.

picture with the buttons for navigation and selecting the defined steps. and

A "callback" message is generated and sent to all recipients. If the recipient has their mailbox in Exchange Online, the original message will be recalled (hard deleted). Furthermore, the message that triggers the callback will deleted. This process is carried out by the "Message Recall Agent" on the Exchange Online Server.

When the recipient's client syncs with the Exchange Online mailbox, the message is never available/visible in the mailbox.

Question: What is zero trust?
Answer: Zero Trust is a new security framework which more effectively adapts to the complexity of the modern environment, embraces the diversity in digital workplace, and protects people, devices, apps, and data wherever they’re located.
AB Answer: Zero Trust is a new security framework that adapts to the complexity of the modern environment and protects people, devices, apps, and data wherever they are located. The main difference between Zero Trust and traditional security architecture is that Zero Trust focuses on protecting data rather than the network. It achieves this through three important principles: explicit verification, least-privilege access, and assuming breach. Zero Trust aims to minimize the blast radius, segment access, and verify end-to-end encryption to improve defenses against cyber threats. It also enables flexibility and freedom in onboarding new solutions, devices, and partners without compromising security. Zero Trust is seen as a key factor in navigating the digital IT landscape with resilience, sparking innovation, securing connections, and boosting collaboration.
Context_paragraphs:
Introducing Zero Trust

Zero Trust is a new security framework which more effectively adapts to the complexity of the modern environment, embraces the diversity in digital workplace, and protects people, devices, apps, and data wherever they’re located.

The biggest difference of Zero Trust to our current security architecture is Zero Trust does not protect network but data. It achieves that with three important principles:
Verify explicitly, Use least-privilege access, assume breach

Question: What are the zero trust principles?
Answer: Verify explicitly, Use least-privilege access, assume breach
AB Answer:
The zero trust principles are as follows:

    Verify explicitly: Always authenticate and authorize based on all available data points, including user identity, location, device health, service or workload, data classification, and anomalies.
    Use least-privilege access: Limit user access with just-in-time and just-enough-access (JIT/JEA), risk-based adaptive policies, and data protection to help secure both data and productivity.
    Assume breach: Minimize blast radius and segment access. Verify end-to-end encryption and use analytics to get visibility, drive threat detection, and improve defenses.

These principles are part of the Zero Trust security framework, which aims to protect data rather than just the network.
